resources.string: Battery not detected: the bike no longer senses the pack
The battery switched itself off after detecting a short circuit; its fuse may have tripped. Check the wiring and the plug at the battery.
The battery’s power switch (MOSFET) is too hot. Let the bike cool down, then try again.
The battery detected a short circuit while switching on. Check the wiring between battery and bike.
The battery detected an overload while switching on. Look for a short circuit in the wiring between battery and bike.
The battery voltage dropped very low. Charge it for longer. If the code stays, the BMS needs a reset (workshop).
The battery voltage is low. Charge the battery.
The battery voltage is too high. Unplug the charger and check that it is the right one (42\u00A0V). A level\u00A02 fault needs a BMS reset.
The battery voltage is too high. Unplug the charger and check that it is the right one (42\u00A0V).
The battery took in too much charging current. Check the charger (42\u00A0V).
Too much charging current. Check the charger (42\u00A0V). A level\u00A02 fault needs a BMS reset.
The bike drew too much current. Look for a short circuit in the wiring or a motor fault. A level\u00A02 fault needs a BMS reset.
The bike briefly drew too much current, for example on a steep hill or with Boost. If it comes back on flat ground, check the motor and its cable.
The battery is too cold to charge. Charge it at room temperature. If the code also shows at normal temperature, a temperature sensor in the battery may be faulty.
The battery is too hot to charge. Let it cool down, then charge. If the code also shows at normal temperature, a temperature sensor in the battery may be faulty.
The battery is too cold to deliver power. Let the bike warm up. If the code also shows at normal temperature, a temperature sensor in the battery may be faulty.
The battery is too hot to deliver power. Let the bike cool down. If the code also shows at normal temperature, a temperature sensor in the battery may be faulty.

The battery reports a permanent failure or does not answer at all. Often its fuse has burned, likely from a short circuit at the battery socket. Check the plug and the socket for burn marks. After that, a workshop has to check the battery.
Battery does not enable charging or discharging
The battery did not switch on its charge or discharge output. Check the battery plug and cable, then restart the bike.

The bike does not see the battery (the detection signal stays low). Check that the battery sits in all the way, then the plug and cable. If 42 shows at the same time, the bike may switch to shipping mode.
The bike cannot talk to the battery over its data line (Modbus). Check the battery plug and cable. If the fault stays, the interface chip in the module or the BMS itself may be defective.
The supply voltage is below 25\u00A0V, as if the battery had switched off its output. Charge the battery and check the battery plug. A short 20 right after a reset is normal.
The bike sees a charger, but no charging current flows. Check the charger (42\u00A0V) and the charging socket. A charge limit that has been reached can cause this too.

The module gets no answer from the motor controller, so there is no assist. While parked, the bike tries to restart it by itself. Switch the bike off and on. If the code stays, the controller has no supply or is defective (workshop).

The module lost contact with its Bluetooth chip and is restarting it, so the app may not connect. You can still unlock with the backup code. If the code stays, the chip or its firmware is defective (workshop).
The firmware transfer from the app was aborted. Restart the bike and start the update again, with the phone close to the bike.
The transferred firmware image failed its checksum. Restart the bike and transfer the update again.
The firmware transfer took too long. Restart the bike and try again with the phone close to the bike.
A file in the update package is missing or invalid. Restart the bike and load the package again.
The module did not finish writing the new firmware in time. Restart the bike and repeat the update. If it fails again, a workshop has to check the module.
The module found no header in the firmware file of the update package. The package is damaged or wrong. Repeat the update with an intact package.
The update package contains no files. Repeat the update with a complete package.
The module could not erase its old firmware. Restart the bike and repeat the update. If it fails again, a workshop has to check the module.
The module could not write the new firmware. Restart the bike and repeat the update. If it fails again, a workshop has to check the module.
A file in the update package has a checksum error. Repeat the update with a fresh package.
The update of the motor controller (motorware) did not finish. Restart the bike and repeat the update. If the motor does not answer afterwards (code\u00A022), a workshop has to recover its firmware.
The update of the battery controller (BMS) did not finish. Restart the bike and repeat the update. If the battery stays silent, a workshop has to flash it again.
The update of the shifter controller did not finish. Restart the bike and repeat the update. If the shifter stays silent (code\u00A044), a workshop has to flash it again.

The update of the Bluetooth controller did not finish. Restart the bike and repeat the update. If the app can no longer connect, you can still unlock with the backup code; a workshop can flash the chip again.

The bike cannot read the small battery inside the smart cartridge; it may be missing, empty or worn out. Charge the bike and check that the module battery charges. If the code stays, replace the module battery.
The module cannot read the ambient light sensor (I²C error), so the automatic light may misbehave. Restart the bike. If the code stays, the module needs a repair.
The bike saw the bell button pressed for more than 20\u00A0s. Clean the button or replace it, and check its cable for moisture or a short circuit.
The bike saw the Boost button pressed for more than 20\u00A0s. Clean the button or replace it, and check its cable for moisture or a short circuit.

The bike cannot detect the coil in the Kick Lock. Usually a plug is loose or a cable is pinched. Please check the Kick Lock plug and follow the cable for kinks. If battery detection fails at the same time, the bike will probably switch to shipping mode.
The shifter tried 10 times and did not reach the gear. Check the shifter cable and plug at the rear hub, then shift again.
The bike got no answer from the shifter five times. Check the shifter plug and cable at the rear hub. If both are fine, the shifter board is probably defective (workshop).
Motor cable or temperature sensor open

The motor temperature sensor (NTC) reads as an open line, as if the motor cable were unplugged or broken. Check the motor plug and the wiring harness to the front wheel for kinks and breaks. If the motor still works, this is often the first sign of a failing harness; without the sensor the motor has no overheat protection. Spin the front wheel: if the speed shows, the speed line is still intact.

The motor driver chip (DRV8301) reported an error. The workshop table says overtemperature, the code’s own name says overcurrent. Let the bike cool down and restart it. If the code returns, check the motor cable for damage; after that, a workshop has to check the controller.
The battery does not report its charge level. Check the battery plug and cable, then restart the bike.

YABA does not count 48 as a fault: the firmware sets this bit from the wheel-speed pulses. The workshop table calls 48 a motor controller error (parameter error, replace motor). If the bike shows 48 on its display or the speed is wrong, check the motor plug and the speed line in the wiring harness.

At start-up the motor controller found a current offset too far from its default value (1.0), so its current measurement is off. Restart the bike. If the code stays, a workshop has to check the controller.
At start-up the motor controller’s voltage measurement was off. Restart the bike and check the battery plug. If the code stays, a workshop has to check the controller.
The motor controller cut the maximum current because it is hot. Let the bike cool down. This is a warning, not a defect.
The motor controller reports a failed torque sensor. Check the plug and cable of the torque sensor and restart the bike.

The motor controller reports a serious fault (parameter error plus not ready) and does not start. Restart the bike once. If the code stays, the workshop table says to replace the motor; have a workshop check motor and controller.
The bike does not detect the SIM card of its tracker, so tracking does not work. Riding is not affected. Check that the SIM sits in its slot and works in another device.
Several chips on the module’s internal I²C bus did not answer at start-up. Restart the bike. If the code stays, the module (smart cartridge) is probably defective.
This is not a VanMoof SIM (its number has the wrong prefix). Insert the SIM that belongs to the bike.
The modem detects the SIM but cannot read it. Take the SIM out, clean its contacts and put it back in. If the code stays, try another VanMoof SIM.
The modem’s start-up failed. Restart the bike; the code often disappears after a reset. If it stays, the modem chip is probably defective (it is easy to replace).
The bike runs its factory firmware instead of the normal firmware. A workshop has to flash the normal firmware again.
This code is not in the fault table. Note the number and when it appears.
The key is invalid. Add the bike to the garage again or reload it.
Bike not found. To wake it, move the bike briefly or press the bell button. The VanMoof app must be closed.
Location is off. Without location, Android cannot find Bluetooth devices.
This is not an S3 or X3, or the Bluetooth cache is corrupted.
Not connected. Please wake the bike and wait a moment.
Android could not open a connection (connectGatt returned null)
No answer from the bike. Usually the bike is asleep, or the VanMoof app is connected to it right now.
Connection interrupted (133). The bike accepts only one connection at a time.
The services of the bike could not be read
The services of the bike could not be read (status %1$s)
Characteristic %1$s is missing on the bike
The bike did not accept %1$d\u00A0km/h (it reports %2$s\u00A0km/h).
The bike did not accept %1$d\u00A0km/h (it reports %2$s\u00A0km/h, region restriction %3$d).
The region of the bike is restricted, so it keeps its speed limit and refused %1$d\u00A0km/h.
The bike did not accept level\u00A0%1$d (it reports %2$s).
This bike does not offer a log.
Kick Lock reports locked while riding
Power/reset button reports pressed while riding
The key vault is not available.
The key vault cannot be read right now. Please restart the app.
The key vault could not be saved.
The sign-in response contained no token.
Session expired. Please sign in again.
The session refresh returned no token.
VanMoof’s server is limiting requests right now. Please wait one minute.
Not signed in, or the session has expired.
You do not have permission for this. Only the owner can do it.
Timed out. The action may have gone through anyway. Please reload the list.
The connection to VanMoof’s server was interrupted.
VanMoof’s server cannot be reached. Please check your internet connection.
Signed out. Your bike keys stay on this phone.
The sound is too long. Choose a shorter one.
The file has no audio track.
This phone cannot decode this format.
The file contains no readable audio data.
Transfer aborted. Please hold the phone close to the bike and send again.
Bluetooth access is missing. Please allow access to nearby devices first.
Connection to the bike interrupted. The bike rides on unchanged, and YABA reconnects.

VanMoof’s server answered with error\u00A0%2$d at %1$s. Your bike is not affected: unlocking, lights, bell and diagnostics run directly over Bluetooth. Only signing in and sharing wait for the server. Tap “Try again” to repeat the request.

At %1$s, no answer came within 10\u00A0seconds. Your bike is not affected: unlocking, lights, bell and diagnostics run directly over Bluetooth. Only signing in and sharing wait for the server. Tap “Try again” to repeat the request.

VanMoof’s server has not answered any request from this phone for %1$d\u00A0days. Your bike does not need it: unlocking, lights, bell and diagnostics keep running directly over Bluetooth. Only signing in and sharing are not possible while the server does not answer.
